selectionMethod: Highest rubric totals within the approved category quotas, followed by deterministic semantic, structure, topic, metadata, factual-safety, and evergreen gates.

discussions.question: Which Disney World attraction gets a wait time its actual experience simply does not justify?
discussions.context: Consider the full experience—not just ride length—including the queue, reliability, atmosphere, and what you give up while waiting.

discussions.question: At what total price does a Disney vacation stop feeling magical and start feeling financially irresponsible?
discussions.context: The line is different for every family. Think about the complete trip cost and what else that money could reasonably buy.

discussions.question: If Disney could restore one retired experience, what current experience would you trade for it?
discussions.context: Nostalgia is easy when nothing has to make room for it. The tradeoff is what makes the answer interesting.

discussions.question: Do the best Disney days start at rope drop, or are guests sacrificing too much sleep for shorter lines?
discussions.context: Compare what an early start saves in line time with what it costs in energy later in the day.

discussions.question: EPCOT has carried several identities. Which should guide its next era: discovery, world culture, festivals, or headline attractions?
discussions.context: The park can contain all four, but priorities reveal what guests believe EPCOT is supposed to be.

discussions.question: Animal Kingdom still gets labeled a half-day park. Is that reputation earned, or does it reveal how people tour it?
discussions.context: A ride checklist and a slower day built around trails, animals, atmosphere, and shows produce very different judgments.

discussions.question: Would you rather accept slower Disney transportation or pay more for control over every trip between parks and hotels?
discussions.context: Buses, boats, gondolas, monorails, rideshares, and rental cars each trade convenience for cost or flexibility.

discussions.question: If one Disney World park had to come off your next itinerary, which would it be—and what would earn its place back?
discussions.context: The second half matters: identify the experience or change that would reverse your decision.

discussions.question: Is a Disney split stay worth changing hotels mid-trip, or does the move erase the benefit?
discussions.context: Trying two resort areas can change transportation and atmosphere, but packing twice has a real cost.

discussions.question: When does staying at a Disney resort justify the premium, and when is an off-site hotel the smarter choice?
discussions.context: Location, transportation, room quality, trip pace, and budget can point to very different answers.

discussions.question: How would you change Hollywood Studios so it feels like a complete, unhurried park day?
discussions.context: Think beyond adding a single ride: capacity, shade, entertainment, dining, and places to slow down all count.

discussions.question: Has planning Disney dining become part of the fun—or homework that gets in the way of the vacation?
discussions.context: Advance choices can protect a must-do meal, but they can also lock a family into a schedule months before hunger arrives.

discussions.question: At what point does park hopping add freedom—and at what point does it simply waste too much vacation time?
discussions.context: The answer changes with trip length, transportation, evening plans, and how much a group values spontaneity.

discussions.question: Paid line-skipping can save hours at Disney. What makes it a smart purchase instead of a frustrating extra charge?
discussions.context: Consider crowd level, group size, trip length, attraction priorities, and whether the saved time actually improves the day.

discussions.question: When does a real pool or rest day improve a Disney trip enough to justify giving up park time?
discussions.context: An extra park day looks valuable on paper. A rested family may remember the trip very differently.

discussions.question: Character dining costs more than a meal. Who is it genuinely worth it for—and who should skip it?
discussions.context: Food, character time, convenience, age, and the value of a guaranteed interaction all belong in the calculation.

discussions.question: A rainy Disney day can clear crowds or derail a plan. What separates a great rain strategy from a miserable one?
discussions.context: Timing, footwear, indoor attractions, expectations, and knowing when to stop can matter more than the forecast itself.

discussions.question: Which Disney queue tells a better story than the attraction waiting at the end of it?
Where does Universal Orlando outperform Disney in ways Disney fans are reluctant to admit?
discussions.context: Compare the guest experience honestly—attractions, hotels, transportation, food, planning, and value are all fair game.

discussions.question: Is Universal still too dependent on screens and simulators, or has that criticism become outdated?
discussions.context: The strongest answer should distinguish between technology used as a shortcut and technology used to create something physical rides cannot.

discussions.question: Does Islands of Adventure have the strongest attraction lineup in Orlando—or too many weak gaps between its headliners?
discussions.context: Judge the whole park day, not only its best-known rides.

discussions.question: At what price does Universal Express stop buying convenience and start feeling like a second admission ticket?
discussions.context: Crowds, trip length, repeat access, and the value of certainty all change the answer.

discussions.question: When a Universal land looks incredible, how much can that make up for attractions you do not want to repeat?
discussions.context: Immersion and repeatable ride quality are both expensive promises. Which one carries more of a return visit?

discussions.question: Would you choose a simpler Universal hotel with effortless park access or a better room that adds transportation time?
What does Universal need to offer more consistently for families whose children are not ready for major thrill rides?
discussions.context: Consider attraction mix, play space, shows, pacing, and whether the whole family can share enough of the day.

discussions.question: Does leaving a Universal park for CityWalk improve a meal—or interrupt the day more than it is worth?
How do you use park-to-park access without turning a Universal day into a rush between headliners?
discussions.context: The goal is not a record ride count; it is a plan that preserves both flexibility and a sense of place.

discussions.question: What must Epic Universe deliver consistently before it becomes the park you build an entire Universal trip around?
discussions.context: A spectacular first visit and a dependable vacation anchor are not necessarily the same thing.

discussions.question: How much should an easy Florida embarkation port influence the cruise you book?
discussions.context: Parking, hotels, traffic, terminal flow, and the trip home can shape a vacation before and after anyone boards the ship.

discussions.question: Would you choose a shorter cruise on a premium ship or more nights on a less exciting one—and why?
discussions.context: Compare the value of time away with the quality of the ship, dining, service, and ports.

discussions.question: What makes a better cruise day: a polished private destination or a port where you experience a real local place?
discussions.context: Convenience and predictability compete with discovery, culture, and the possibility of a less controlled day.

discussions.question: When should loyalty to a cruise line lose to a better itinerary or ship?
discussions.context: Status perks and familiarity are valuable, but they can quietly narrow the trips a traveler considers.

discussions.question: Which Florida itinerary looks reasonable on a map but turns into far too much driving in real life?
discussions.context: Florida distances, traffic, parking, and the energy required for each stop can make an ambitious route feel very different on the road.

discussions.question: How much inconvenience will you tolerate for a Florida beach town that still feels distinctive?
discussions.context: Parking, price, crowds, walkability, and local character rarely point toward the same destination.

discussions.question: Which Florida attraction do locals dismiss too quickly, and what makes it worth defending?
discussions.context: Skip the automatic tourist-trap label. Make the case for the experience, place, or tradition that earns a second look.

discussions.question: Which Florida experience deserves more than a day trip to understand properly?
